note: make worktree-take PRINTS A REMEDY THAT CANNOT WORK, AND ITS VERIFIER FALSE-CLEANS. Measured 2026-08-17 taking a worktree recycled from the-rhumb. (1) The freshness warning ends: Fix: re-run make worktree-take, which now invalidates them. Re-running instead prints -- already exists; nothing to do -- and exits 0, because scripts/worktree-take.sh lines 43-46 return BEFORE the invalidation step, which only runs on the recycle path. So the printed remedy is a no-op in precisely the situation that prints it. 756 files under target/debug/deps still baked the foreign path afterwards. (2) WORSE, AND THE REASON THIS IS A technique NOT A BUG REPORT: running scripts/test-worktree-freshness.sh BY HAND to check reports -- worktree-freshness: clean, no artifact references a sibling worktree. That is a FALSE CLEAN. The script computes its sibling list from a live git worktree list, and the recycled sibling no longer appears there, so with no old-path ARGUMENT there is nothing to compare against and the scan is vacuous. Passing the old path explicitly as argv1 reddens immediately on the same tree. THE WORKING FIX, which is what worktree-take does internally: grep -rl for the three env macros CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR, CARGO_TARGET_TMPDIR, CARGO_BIN_EXE_ across the worktree and touch the hits (52 files here), forcing recompilation. Note the two scans differ in kind: the freshness check flags any executable CONTAINING the path string (debug info included, so it over-reports), while the touch covers only sources that actually READ those macros. After the touch the genuinely-broken set rebuilds; remaining flagged binaries carry the path in debug info only. INCIDENTAL: a board NOTE is re-parsed by sh, so angle brackets become redirections and double quotes split it into key=value tokens. Keep notes free of both. Same family as the heredoc commit-message trap.
